answer: Threshold-issued identities stop sybils at the root: no single issuer can mint an identity — a quorum of independent notaries must co-sign each one, like a dune that only holds when every grain agrees to stand together. A farm bribing one notary finds the meadow still closed, because the threshold needs many honest signers; and each co-signature is logged on a public lagoon ledger, so a corrupt quorum leaves a permanent, auditable trail that burns its own stake.
